overview: Zhejiang Expressway is a PRC state-controlled infrastructure company that invests in, develops and operates nine toll expressways and bridges totaling roughly 1,050 km, mostly in Zhejiang Province (one in Anhui), connecting core cities of the Yangtze River Delta and the port of Ningbo-Zhoushan. Since 2017 it has also owned a controlling stake in Zheshang Securities (listed on the Shanghai Stock Exchange), which has grown into a near-equal second pillar of revenue and now contributes over half of group net profit. The Company is majority-owned (via H and domestic shares) by Zhejiang Communications Investment Group, a provincial state-owned enterprise, and is dual-listed with H Shares on HKEX since 1997, with an A-share listing (via absorption of Zhejiang Oceanking Development) pending CSRC/SSE approval as of late 2026.

business_model.summary: Toll road operation is a regulated, capital-intensive, highly cash-generative annuity-like business funded by government-set per-kilometre toll rates; securities brokerage/trading (Zheshang Securities) is a more cyclical, capital-markets-linked business that now rivals tolls in revenue scale and exceeds it in profit contribution. A smaller 'other business' segment includes construction services, hotels/catering and PPP projects.

revenue_streams.name: Toll road operations (9 expressways)
revenue_streams.trend: declining (diversion from new competing roads, ETC toll discounts, reconstruction traffic control)

revenue_streams.name: Securities business (Zheshang Securities)
revenue_streams.trend: growing strongly (capital markets recovery, M&A activity, Guodu Securities consolidation)

revenue_streams.name: Other (construction services, hotels, PPP)
revenue_streams.trend: growing (construction service revenue up sharply on project work)

business_model.customer_type: B2C/mixed infrastructure user base (motorists and freight operators) for tolls; B2B/B2C brokerage, wealth management and institutional clients for securities
business_model.geographic_mix: Toll roads: almost entirely Zhejiang Province, PRC (one expressway in Anhui); Securities: mainland China with a small Hong Kong subsidiary presence (Zheshang/Guodu HK entities); reporting currency Rmb, H Shares trade in HKD

main_competitors: China Merchants Expressway Network & Technology (001965.SZ) — also a shareholder in several of the Company's project subsidiaries
Other provincial toll-road operators and newly opened competing/parallel expressways within Zhejiang
In securities: CITIC Securities, Guotai Junan/Haitong (merged), GF Securities, and other national/regional brokers competing with Zheshang Securities
competitive_position.market_position: Dominant incumbent operator of expressways within Zhejiang Province, one of China's wealthiest and most trade-intensive provinces; a mid-sized but growing national securities franchise via Zheshang Securities (enlarged by the Guodu Securities acquisition) within China's highly fragmented, policy-driven brokerage industry

moat_factors.description: Toll road concessions are granted by provincial government and cannot be freely replicated; the Company holds long-dated, government-sanctioned rights to collect tolls on strategic Zhejiang corridors

Expressways connect major economic centers (Shanghai-Hangzhou-Ningbo corridor, Ningbo-Zhoushan Port) with limited practical substitute routes for freight and commuters, supporting durable traffic demand

Controlling shareholder is the provincial government's transportation investment arm, providing access to project pipelines, financing support and acquisition opportunities (e.g., Guisan, Yonglan expressways) but also subjecting the Company to policy directives (toll discounts) that pressure revenue
A controlling stake in a Shanghai-listed securities firm gives counter-cyclical/diversified earnings and capital markets optionality not available to pure-play toll operators

weaknesses: No pricing power: toll rates are regulated and subject to mandated discounts (5% ETC discount, 15% ETC truck discount expanded in 2025) that directly erode revenue

Traffic diversion risk from new parallel/competing roads opening nearby (Suzhou-Taizhou Expressway Phase II, Hangzhou-Shaoxing-Ningbo Expressway, National Highway 329 upgrades all cited as causing declines in FY2025/H1 2026)
Earnings increasingly dependent on the more volatile, capital-markets-correlated securities segment, diluting the defensive, annuity-like character of the original toll business
Complex related-party structure with controlling shareholder (construction, finance, HR services all transacted with Communications Group entities) raises governance/connected-transaction scrutiny
Concession assets are finite-life (amortizing); some sections face declining remaining operating years, requiring reinvestment or renewal/extension negotiations with the government

growth_drivers: Pending A-share listing via absorption/merger with Zhejiang Oceanking Development (share swap, CSRC registration approved June 30, 2026) — intended to unlock valuation recovery and broaden access to mainland capital

Expressway M&A via the 'Zhijiang Communications Holdings' investment platform: completed 51% stake in Guisan Expressway (135km, Guangxi) in 2025, following earlier acquisition of Yonglan Expressway (145km, Hunan) — expanding geographic footprint beyond Zhejiang

Reconstruction and expansion of existing expressways (Jinhua/Shaoxing sections of Ningbo-Jinhua Expressway, Zhajiasu Expressway, Shanghai-Hangzhou-Ningbo Expressway feasibility study) to add capacity and support long-term toll growth
New investment win: Parallel Line of Ningbo-Zhoushan Expressway Phase II project (with Ningbo Zhoushan Port and local government partners)
Securities business expansion: Zheshang Securities' acquisition of a controlling stake in Guodu Securities, pursuing a national medium-to-large brokerage strategy via both organic growth and M&A

'Second growth curve' initiatives: transportation + energy integration (photovoltaic along expressways, EV truck battery-swap stations, green/low-carbon toll stations), intelligent/autonomous-driving-enabled expressway technology, and early-stage low-altitude economy integration

Resilient Zhejiang Province economy (GDP +5.5% in 2025, +5.7% in H1 2026, both above national average) driven by private sector, digital economy and foreign trade, providing an organic growth underpin for toll traffic

business.description: Multiple newly-opened or expanding parallel/competing roads (Suzhou-Taizhou Expressway Phase II, Hangzhou-Shaoxing-Ningbo Expressway, National Highway 329) are structurally diverting traffic from several of the Group's expressways (Zhajiasu -27% H1 2026 toll revenue, Jinhua section -36%)
Government-directed ETC discounts (5% general, 15% truck discount expanded province-wide from April 2025) directly reduce toll revenue regardless of traffic volume growth

Ongoing reconstruction and expansion projects on the Group's own and connecting external road networks cause temporary lane closures and traffic control, denting toll revenue during construction (multi-year horizon to 2028)
Commission/fee income and trading gains at Zheshang Securities are tied to capital market trading volumes and sentiment, introducing earnings volatility atypical of the legacy toll business

business.risk: Execution risk on Oceanking merger/A-share listing
business.description: Complex cross-border/cross-exchange share-swap and new A-share issuance subject to multiple regulatory approvals, integration risk, and potential dilution

financial.description: Gearing ratio rose from 129.0% (Dec 2024) to 137.6% (Dec 2025) to 147.6% (June 2026); asset-liability ratio rose from 66.1% to 68.3% to 72.2% over the same period, driven by expansion capex, acquisitions and securities-business balance sheet growth
Total interest-bearing borrowings rose 29.6% YoY to Rmb71.6bn at Dec 2025 and further to Rmb85.1bn by June 2026, partly in floating-rate instruments exposed to rate changes
Interest cover ratio slipped from 7.5x (H1 2025) to 7.1x (H1 2026), still comfortable but trending down as debt grows faster than EBIT
No interim dividend declared for H1 2026, a departure that could unsettle income-focused H-share holders even if full-year payout is maintained

regulatory.description: Provincial/national toll discount mandates (ETC discounts) are a direct, non-negotiable earnings risk entirely outside management's control

The Oceanking absorption-merger and A-share issuance require ongoing regulatory approvals (SSE review completed May 2026, CSRC registration approved June 30, 2026, valid 12 months) — any delay, condition or withdrawal could disrupt the value-unlock thesis
Tightening regulatory scrutiny of China's brokerage industry (capital requirements, fee compression, consolidation pressure) affects Zheshang Securities' margins and strategy
Extensive related-party dealings with controlling shareholder Communications Group (financial services, construction, HR, deposits) require ongoing Hong Kong Listing Rules compliance and disclosure

macro.description: Toll revenue is explicitly linked to GDP and trade activity; a slowdown in China's (4.7% H1 2026 national GDP growth) or Zhejiang's economy, or in export-driven freight demand via Ningbo-Zhoushan Port, would directly reduce traffic and toll revenue
Management repeatedly cites geopolitical conflict and international trade frictions as disrupting energy markets, supply chains and freight demand feeding the expressway network
A meaningful share of borrowings carry floating rates (~Rmb15.5bn) and the Group is a large net borrower, making it rate-sensitive, though PRC rates have generally been easing
Operations are almost entirely RMB-denominated; H-share dividends paid in HKD and a USD470m senior bond (repaid July 2026) created modest historical FX exposure, now reduced

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Chinese toll-road industry is mature and low-growth in traffic terms but provides stable, government-protected cash flows; growth now depends on M&A/network expansion, reconstruction-driven capacity, and diversification into adjacent infrastructure services (energy, intelligent transport) rather than organic traffic growth alone. China's securities industry is undergoing state-directed consolidation (mirroring the Guotai Haitong mega-merger), favoring brokers with government-linked ownership and capital strength like Zheshang Securities.
macro_factors.cyclicality: Toll business: low-to-moderate cyclicality, correlated with regional GDP/trade volumes, cushioned by regulated structure; Securities business: moderate-to-high cyclicality, directly correlated with mainland capital market trading activity, IPO/M&A volumes and investor sentiment
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Moderate — significant debt load (~Rmb85bn interest-bearing borrowings at June 2026) with a mix of fixed and floating rate instruments; lower PRC rates would ease interest costs, but securities business margin-lending/trading book also has rate sensitivity
key_input_costs: Construction and maintenance costs for expressway reconstruction/expansion
Borrowing costs (bank loans, corporate bonds, short-term financing notes)
Capital market-linked costs for securities business (compensation tied to trading/commission revenue)

recent_developments.event: H1 2026 interim results: revenue +21.0% YoY to Rmb10,508.17m (boosted by securities business +42.1% YoY and construction services +250%), but profit attributable to owners fell 3.2% YoY to Rmb2,697.20m on declining toll revenue (-5.4%) and rising leverage; no interim dividend declared
USD470 million senior fixed-rate bonds (coupon 1.638%) issued in 2021 were repaid in full on July 14, 2026, reducing the Group's limited USD exposure

China Securities Regulatory Commission (CSRC) granted registration approval for the Oceanking Development absorption-merger and associated A-share issuance (up to ~541 million new A shares), valid for 12 months — a major milestone toward the Company's long-planned dual H-share/A-share listing
Shanghai Stock Exchange review committee confirmed the Oceanking absorption-merger and concurrent A-share issuance complies with reorganization and disclosure requirements
JPMorgan reiterated a Hold rating with an HK$7.20 price target (May 6, 2026)

Extraordinary shareholders' meeting approved the Oceanking merger plan, a three-year post-merger shareholder dividend return plan, and abolition of the supervisory committee (corporate governance simplification)
Entered into absorption-and-merger agreement with Zhejiang Oceanking Development via A-share swap (1.08 Zhejiang Expressway shares per Oceanking share, per market reports), targeting dual A+H listing
All outstanding 2021 convertible bonds (EUR-denominated, stock code 40526) fully converted into H Shares; bonds delisted from HKEX

Completed acquisition of 51% equity stake in the 135km Guisan Expressway (Guangxi) via the Zhijiang Communications Holdings joint-venture platform, extending the Group's expressway footprint beyond Zhejiang (following the earlier Yonglan Expressway acquisition in Hunan)

Zheshang Securities' consolidation of its controlling stake in Guodu Securities contributed to a 22.1% YoY increase in FY2025 securities revenue, with brokerage and securities investment income particularly strong

guidance.as_of: H1 2026 Interim Report (August 2026) and FY2025 Annual Report Outlook (March 2026)

items.target: Continued organic growth supported by Zhejiang's GDP outperformance
items.notes: Management does not give numeric toll revenue guidance; qualitative outlook flags continued phased traffic-control impacts from reconstruction/expansion projects and competing-road diversion through at least 2028

items.notes: To be funded first from internal resources, then debt/equity financing as needed

items.target: Remaining ~Rmb3,950 million of rights issue proceeds: ~Rmb2,330m for expressway reconstruction/expansion (phased Rmb940m/Rmb940m/Rmb450m through Dec 2028) and ~Rmb1,620m for working capital/debt repayment (fully utilized by July 31, 2026, per H1 2026 report)
items.vs_prior: reallocated (Dec 31, 2025 board approval shifted remaining proceeds from pure capex toward liquidity/debt repayment)
items.notes: Confirms a conservative, internally-funded approach to capex pacing

items.target: Complete absorption-merger and dual listing on SSE (A shares) and HKEX (H shares)
items.period: FY2026 (CSRC approval valid 12 months from June 30, 2026)
items.vs_prior: advancing — raised in priority/certainty since CSRC registration approval
items.notes: A three-year post-merger shareholder dividend return plan was approved at the March 2026 EGM, implying explicit multi-year capital return commitments tied to deal completion

items.target: Build Zheshang Securities into a 'national medium-to-large securities firm' via endogenous growth and further M&A
items.notes: No specific revenue/profit targets disclosed; strategy continues to lean on the Guodu Securities integration

guidance.management_commentary: Chairman Yuan Yingjie's statement frames 2026 as the inaugural year of the 15th Five-Year Plan, with strategic orientation of 'expanding growth, extending existing business, activating dynamic variables and stabilizing profitability levels.' Management explicitly prioritizes advancing the A-share listing to 'facilitate valuation recovery,' pursuing a 'second growth curve' in transportation-energy integration, intelligent transportation and the low-altitude economy, while acknowledging toll revenue will face continued phased pressure from reconstruction traffic control and road-network diversion into FY2026-2028.

bull_case: Pending A-share listing (Oceanking absorption-merger, CSRC-approved June 2026) could unlock a valuation re-rating, given the stock's low single-digit P/E (~6.2x trailing) and the typical A-share premium over H-shares for comparable state-owned infrastructure names

Diversified, growing securities business (Zheshang Securities + Guodu Securities) gives exposure to China's capital market recovery and brokerage consolidation theme, with H1 2026 segment revenue up 42% YoY, increasingly offsetting toll-business softness

Expressway network is irreplaceable, government-protected infrastructure located in economically resilient Zhejiang Province (GDP growth consistently above national average), providing a durable base of cash flow and dividends
Active, government-backed M&A pipeline (Guisan, Yonglan expressway acquisitions; Ningbo-Zhoushan Parallel Line Phase II win) extends the growth runway beyond organic Zhejiang traffic
Shareholder-friendly state-owned enterprise with historically high dividend payout and an explicit three-year post-merger dividend return plan committed by the board
bear_case: Core toll business is in structural decline on several key routes due to new competing roads, mandated ETC discounts and reconstruction traffic control, with H1 2026 toll revenue down 5.4% YoY and some sections down over 25-36%

Rising leverage (gearing ratio up from 129% to 147.6% in 18 months; asset-liability ratio up to 72.2%) alongside falling interest cover signals increasing financial risk as the Group funds acquisitions and securities-business growth with debt
Earnings quality is being diluted by growing reliance on the more volatile, trading-sentiment-driven securities segment, undermining the historically defensive, annuity-like investment case
Execution risk around the complex Oceanking absorption-merger and A-share listing — regulatory, integration or market-timing setbacks could delay or dilute the anticipated valuation benefits
No interim dividend was declared for H1 2026 (versus H1 2025), a potential early signal of capital discipline tightening or payout policy change that could disappoint income-oriented investors

Heavy related-party transaction network with the controlling shareholder (Zhejiang Communications Investment Group) raises governance and minority-shareholder-alignment concerns typical of PRC state-owned enterprises
